shocks._conservation_note: Zero-sum transfer: consumer losses (JP_KR+EU=0.18) exactly match producer gains (GULF+RU=0.18) -- an energy price shock reallocates value, it doesn't create or destroy it.
Net destruction (-0.20, tracked): a chip supply-chain disruption destroys real value (idled fabs, broken contracts) rather than transferring it to a named winner.
Small net destruction (-0.02, tracked): deadweight loss typical of a bailout/fire-sale, not a clean transfer.
Zero-sum transfer: crop-loss regions (ST_FRAGILE+HH_EM_SUBSIST=-0.05) lose exactly what unaffected exporters (ST_SWING=+0.05) gain via higher prices.
Zero-sum transfer (debt haircut): creditor write-downs (IFI+AM_ACTIVE=-0.10) exactly fund the debtor's relief (ST_FRAGILE=+0.10) -- a real restructuring transfers the loss, it doesn't vaporize it.
No resources effect (liquidity/security only) -- trivially conserved.
No resources effect (legitimacy/autonomy/security only) -- trivially conserved.
No resources effect (liquidity/security only) -- trivially conserved.

shocks._source_note: Represents the faster branch of a genuinely disputed range: LEAP Wave 8 (2026) superforecaster median for 8hr-task-level AI is ~2028 vs public median ~2037 (forecastingresearch.org/leap). Not a consensus forecast, one branch of one.
shocks._conservation_note: Zero-sum transfer: capital-allocation gains to the AI complex (CORP_TECH+CORP_SEMI+CORP_ENERGY=+0.23) are funded by capital reallocated away from diversified/traditional portfolios (AM_ACTIVE=-0.13) and by labor's wage share not keeping pace with productivity (HH_DM_LABOR=-0.10) -- AI capex isn't free money, it's a real reallocation.

shocks._source_note: 2026 AI capex >$700B, ~23% of hyperscaler revenue, actively debated as bubble risk (Bridgewater, Forbes Aug 2026). Probability rises after sustained AI-driven gains (CORP_TECH rank) rather than being independent of them, per the skill's correlated-shock rule.
shocks._conservation_note: Net destruction (-0.22, tracked): a correction destroys paper wealth built on unrealized productivity gains -- HF_MACRO's small gain (variance-preferring short-side profit) doesn't fully offset the loss.

shocks._source_note: NBER survey (2026): 90% of firms report zero measurable AI productivity impact despite heavy capex; labor market shows no major shakeup yet (computer/math occupations +5.7% since 2023). Modeled as the modal, low-drama branch rather than the shock headlines cover.
shocks._conservation_note: Small net destruction (-0.07, tracked): capex spent without a productivity payoff is real waste, not a transfer to anyone.

shocks._source_note: IFR (2026): China installs 54% of world industrial robots, operational stock ~2M units (4.5x Japan), robotics now central to China's 15th Five-Year Plan as an explicit growth driver. South Korea leads world robot density (1220/10k workers vs Western Europe's 267). Humanoid robotics raised $18.8bn in H1 2026 alone (vs $15bn all of 2025), Goldman reports 40% YoY manufacturing-cost decline for humanoids. WEF: automation displaces an estimated 85M jobs by 2030 gross (97M created net) -- near-term dislocation is real even though the net effect is projected positive.
shocks._conservation_note: Zero-sum transfer: manufacturing productivity gains (ST_CN+ST_JP_KR+CORP_TECH+CORP_DEFENSE=+0.19) come from labor's compressed wage/informal-income share (HH_DM_LABOR+HH_EM_URBAN=-0.19), consistent with the WEF's own near-term-dislocation finding.

shocks._source_note: Humanoid robotics priced by Morgan Stanley at a $5tn eventual market on H1-2026 funding pace ($18.8bn) that already exceeds all of 2025 -- a venture-heavy, hype-sensitive pattern comparable to the AI capex debate. Probability rises after sustained AI/robotics-driven CORP_TECH gains rather than independently of them, same correlated-shock logic as ai_capex_correction.
shocks._conservation_note: Net destruction (-0.18, tracked): same logic as ai_capex_correction -- a venture-funding correction destroys speculative paper value, it isn't captured by a named winner.
